summary: AccessControl.Properties docstring claimed raw fidelity that the schema's own promotion + decoding rules contradict
verifier_finding: Name is now lifted out and PropertyDecoder rewrites NotDefault values in place; saying Properties is 'exactly as Access wrote it' and round-trips faithfully is no longer true.
fix: Rewrote AccessControl.Properties documentation to enumerate the two sanctioned mutations: (1) promoted exact-value keys (Name on AccessControl; RecordSource/Filter/OrderBy on form/report roots) are removed when non-null; (2) PropertyDecoder rewrites NotDefault values in place and surfaces the affected keys in NonDefaultProperties. Decoded-lift fields (DefaultView) are explicitly noted as keeping their raw numeric code in Properties.

summary: AccessControl.VbaCode was redundant given the acyclic-by-reference contract
verifier_finding: FormMetadata and ReportMetadata already carry top-level VbaCode. The acyclic-by-reference contract forbids inlining a form/report root as a Children node, so AccessControl.VbaCode has no valid population point in this schema.
fix: Removed VbaCode from AccessControl. VbaCode now lives only on the form/report root types. Aligns with the acyclic-by-reference contract — no schema path produces an AccessControl node that would carry VBA.

summary: GeometryInches remarks misstated where the unit is encoded
verifier_finding: The remarks said 'unit is in the field name', but the unit is in the containing record/field name (GeometryIn / GeometryInches), not in the X/Y/W/H field names themselves.
fix: Reworded the remarks: the unit is encoded in the containing record/field name (GeometryIn / GeometryInches), and the coordinate fields stay short.
